description: "Resolve the saved request before starting another change." does not say what the saved request is. Here it was a handoff of this task to Setup agent with status Review, made before a reload.
expected: Name the pending change, such as "Your handoff of 'Apple Pay sheet freezes on iOS 17' to Setup agent (Review) hasn't been confirmed.", with Retry next to it.
actual: A generic sentence and Retry saved request.
suggested_fix: Render a summary from the pending record (type, task title, key fields) in both the page notice and the panel notice.

description: A pending request cannot be discarded. The only action is Retry saved request, and every other change is refused until the retry succeeds. If the server will never accept it (for example after REVOKED or FORBIDDEN), the only way out is clearing site data or closing the tab.
expected: A secondary "Discard this change" action, with a short warning that the change may already have reached Pardner and that History shows the truth.
suggested_fix: Add a discard action that clears the pending sessionStorage entry after a confirmation.

description: When the retry succeeds, the notice disappears and the task moves, but no confirmation such as "Handed off to Setup agent · agent · Review" is shown.
expected: A short success line after a replay, so the person knows which change landed.
suggested_fix: Show a transient confirmation naming the replayed operation.

description: Comment timestamps use "11/9/2026, 11:42:56 AM", and History in the same panel uses "Nov 9, 2026, 11:42 AM".
expected: One date format across the panel.
suggested_fix: Use the shared date formatter for comments.

description: Add comment (and the quick Status select) look available while a request is pending, and are refused only after the click.
expected: Disabled with the reason shown beside them, or the comment queued after the pending request.
actual: Enabled, then refused after the click.
suggested_fix: Disable mutation controls while pending, the same way as New task, with an inline hint.
